title: Rabbi Chanina or Chananyah son of Rabbi Hillel

paragraphs: Rabbi Chanina (or Chananyah), son of Rabbi Hillel.

Hyman finds him only in halakhic discussions of the Jerusalem Talmud: as Rabbi Chanina son of Rabbi Hillel in Challah 3:3, Shabbat 3:3, Chagigah 2:5 and Avodah Zarah 3:7; and as Rabbi Chananyah son of Rabbi Hillel in Sheviit 1:3, Terumot 1:2 and 4:3, Orlah 1:3, Shabbat 1:5, Megillah 4:7 and Yoma 8:7. At the end of Shabbat 3:3 he discusses Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose’s disagreement. Terumot 4:3 has him saying, “The Mishnah says so,” followed by “Rabbi Chinena said: Interpret it…” Hyman identifies him in all these places as Rabbi Chananyah, Rabbi Mana’s colleague. If so, he belonged to the fifth generation of Palestinian Amoraim.

notes.text: The different spellings Chanina, Chananyah and Chinena remain. The fifth-generation date is Hyman’s conditional inference from companionship with Mana; it is not a newly verified chronology.

The direct Chananyah son of Hillel/Yonah–Yose discussion was read in whole Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat chapter 3 and independently confirmed at 3:5 in the consulted division, versus Hyman’s supplied 3:3. The supplied locator remains unchanged. Chanina/Chananyah/Chinena forms, the only-halakhah assertion, equation of occurrences and conditional Mana-era chronology remain Hyman’s claims.
